goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — Requiring a non-null user suppresses conditional-passkey form setup on the initial anonymous login, removing passkey authentication there.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at line 160 returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This is used in `authenticate()` and `challenge()` methods. Looking at the diff, in `authenticate()` the passkey form setup was moved outside the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block, so it now runs when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true. For initial anonymous login where user is null, this condition returns false, but the original code also only set up passkeys when `context.getUser() == null` AND `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. The new code structure actually maintains similar behavior - passkeys are set up when appropriate. The tests in the diff show passkey authentication working correctly on initial login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:293 — The broad catch treats any WebDriver/page failure as proof that the WebAuthn form is absent, so this negative assertion can silently pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 293 a broad 'catch (Exception nsee)' block that catches any exception to verify the WebAuthn form is absent. This is a real code quality concern - using a generic Exception catch for a negative assertion could mask other failures (like timing issues, page load problems, etc.) and cause the test to pass incorrectly. However, this is not a bug in the application code itself, but rather a test quality issue that could lead to false positives in the test suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:52 — No re-authentication test exercises a failed conditional-passkey challenge, leaving the newly changed error-path form state unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new code at line 52 in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java that calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) in the createErrorResponse method. This is a new error-handling path for conditional passkey failures. Looking at the test files added, the tests (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, etc.) all test successful passkey authentication during re-authentication, but none of them test the scenario where a conditional passkey challenge fails during re-authentication. The finding correctly identifies that this new error-path code is not covered by the added tests.
